content.user_title: Configure Network Isolation for AI Coding
content.value_statement: AI coding tools need controlled network access to reduce data leaks and malicious downloads. This skill helps define trusted domains, proxy settings, and safe environment variable rules.
actual_capabilities: Select trusted, custom, or no-network sandbox modes.
Build trusted domain lists for registries, source control, CDNs, and internal services.
Plan corporate proxy and no-proxy settings for enterprise environments.
Separate safe configuration variables from secrets that belong outside sandbox settings.
Define validation checks for allowed and blocked network access.
Document threats mitigated by deny-by-default network rules.
limitations: It provides configuration guidance, not a runnable enforcement engine.
It depends on the host tool supporting sandbox network controls.
It cannot verify private domains without user-provided environment details.
It does not replace formal enterprise security review.

use_cases.title: Open Source Development
use_cases.description: Allow package registries and GitHub while blocking unrelated outbound network access.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Sandbox Policy
use_cases.description: Define internal registries, proxy settings, and trusted public services for controlled AI coding work.

use_cases.title: Sensitive Project Isolation
use_cases.description: Choose no-network or strict custom access for projects with confidential code or regulated data.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Trusted Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for common development work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure trusted network access for a JavaScript project. Allow npm, GitHub, and common CDNs. Keep secrets out of sandbox settings.

prompt_templates.title: No-Network Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a no-network sandbox policy for a sensitive repository. Include validation steps and explain what workflows may fail.

prompt_templates.title: Enterprise Custom Domains
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom network policy. Include our internal registry, documentation site, corporate proxy, and only required public registries.

prompt_templates.title: Threat-Driven Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of network and secret exposure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sandbox access plan against prompt injection, malware downloads, data exfiltration, and internal network scanning risks.

output_examples.input: Set up safe network access for an open-source Node project.
output_examples.output: The response recommends trusted mode, permits npm and GitHub access, blocks unknown domains, and lists tests for package install and denied access.

output_examples.input: Create an enterprise policy with a corporate proxy and internal registry.
output_examples.output: The response identifies required internal domains, proxy entries, public registry exceptions, and secret handling notes for local environment files.

output_examples.input: Review whether our sandbox policy protects secrets.
output_examples.output: The response flags secrets that should not appear in sandbox settings and explains how network denial reduces exfiltration risk.

best_practices: Start with deny-by-default access, then add only required domains.
Document secret names without storing secret values in sandbox configuration.
Test both allowed package operations and blocked untrusted destinations.
anti_patterns: Allowing broad wildcard domains without a clear business need.
Putting API keys, database URLs, or private keys in sandbox settings.
Skipping validation after changing proxy or trusted domain rules.

faq.question: Does this skill enforce network blocking itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides policy design for tools that already support sandbox network controls.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for Claude Code sandbox planning and also describes patterns useful for Codex workflows.

faq.question: Should secrets be listed in sandbox settings?
faq.answer: No. List required secret names only, and keep real values in approved secret storage.

faq.question: When should I choose no-network mode?
faq.answer: Use no-network mode for highly sensitive work, offline tasks, or projects that do not need package downloads.

faq.question: How are internal registries handled?
faq.answer: The skill helps add exact internal registry domains, ports, and proxy exceptions based on your environment.

faq.question: Does it include validation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests checks for allowed registries, blocked untrusted domains, proxy behavior, and missing environment variables.
